parsed.impact: Per-category shuffled deck without repeats, saved as one JSON file per key through the new `src/storage.ts` and resumed on reopen; unit and Maestro coverage is in place and the gates pass, with only the emulator acceptance run still pending. The new direct `expo-file-system` dependency is classed critical (DEC-54), so the PR waits for the owner.

findings.text: src/storage.ts:20 — `save` has no try/catch while `load` does. A failed write (disk full, unwritable file) throws inside the press handler (`markSeen`) or the `useState` initializer (`openDeck`), which crashes the card screen, whereas an unreadable file is handled gracefully → wrap the write in try/catch and treat a failed save as "progress not remembered", or state in DEC-54 that crashing is accepted.

src/storage.ts:21 — `File.write` on Android truncates and then writes in place (`outputStream(append=false)`), so a kill mid-write leaves an empty or partial file. That reads back as unreadable and the deck restarts with a new shuffle, losing progress and allowing repeats. The window is tiny with a ~1 KB file → either write to `<key>.json.tmp` and move it over, or note the accepted risk in DEC-54.

src/progress.ts:77 — When the last card is passed, `openDeck` reshuffles with no check against the last seen question. With probability 1/n the first card of the new shuffle is the one just shown, which breaks the story's "never the same question twice in a row". DEC-55 makes this an interim state until US-03-03 → optionally reshuffle once if `order[0]` equals the last seen id, or leave it to US-03-03 and say so in the story.

src/app/__tests__/cards.test.tsx:226 — The screen-level "each question once (#1)" test uses a 2-card deck with a mocked, deterministic `Math.random`, so it would pass even with a broken shuffle. The real check is the 50-card test in progress.test.ts:139 plus Maestro TC-03-07 → no change needed, but TC-03-07 to TC-03-11 on the emulator should be green before merge.
